description: Turn a CSV into posts with AI: each row becomes a post written from the prompt, keeping names, links and hashtags from the row, and image/video links in a row can be attached as media. Without schedule every post is saved as a draft. With schedule, rows with a future date and time are scheduled at it and will publish automatically, so confirm with the user before scheduling. Dates are read from the file, not guessed: one cell like "2027-10-21 18:26", "21/10/2027 6:26 pm", "Oct 21, 2027 18:26" or ISO 8601 with an offset, or a date column plus a time column. Rows dated in the past or without a readable date become drafts. Files over 50 rows are sent in parts automatically (500 rows max). Uses 1 AI generation per started block of 25 rows from the daily quota. Requires an active subscription.

csv.description: The CSV text, header row first. Give this or file_path.

file_path.description: Absolute path to a .csv file on disk. Give this or csv.

group_name.description: Label for this batch of posts. Default: the file name.

prompt.description: How the AI should turn each row into a post, e.g. "Write a birthday tribute for each artist with their best-known song. Attach the image."

date_column.description: Header of the column with the date (or the date and time)

order.description: How a date like 03/04/2027 reads: dmy = 3 April, mdy = March 4. Defaults from the timezone.

time_column.description: Header of a separate time column, if the time is not in the date cell

schedule.description: true finds the date/time columns on its own; or name them. Omit to create drafts only.

timezone.description: IANA timezone the times in the file are in, e.g. "Europe/London". Default: the account timezone setting, else UTC.

x_account_id.description: Target X account ID (for multi-account users)

name: opentweet_import_csv
